_doc: The Arkiv act's clock (frames at 60 fps), read by Act.tsx and prep/sponsors/arkiv.py so picture and sound agree. 'pre' shots are absolute; the field-report clips (built.json clips with sponsor ARKIV) start at 'clips' and push everything in 'post' (relative to the clips' end) later. 'lines' are [shot, offset, len, text, text once built.arkiv is true]; at most 2.8 words a second. ghost1/ghost2 are the real ghost races (public/sponsors/arkiv/ghost, prep/sponsors/arkiv_ghosts.py); *In keys are cut-ins inside a shot.
lines: With Arkiv, the Any% board is public data, not our database.
Every run our checker verifies becomes an Arkiv entity.
Its attributes are the record: game, time, log hash, who checked it.
The console's board reads those rows back from Arkiv.
The ghost just ahead of you is one query: frames under your best.
That query finds you her ghost.
It replays her log beside you.
The gap comes from both logs.
Anyone can run the same query, with no key.
Anyone can write a row that looks like ours, with a better time.
The board only counts rows created by our checker's key.
Arkiv stamps every row with the wallet that wrote it.
Runs stay on the board until 30 days after the season.
Anyone can keep a ghost alive.
A run row can't be edited, even by us.
The Mumbai build: the checker writes, every board reads.
Built at ETHGlobal Mumbai: the checker writes, every board reads.
Anyone runs the board's query, on rows only our checker could write.
